problems.text: Finding meeting time is slow and fragmented
Customers check multiple calendars and send back-and-forth emails to find a time
Copy-paste calendar links do not auto-update if the host's availability changes

proposed_solutions.text: Integrate with the Google and Outlook calendar APIs and show available time

user_segments.text: Customers whose setups differ: some use Google Calendar, some Outlook, some both
Enterprise accounts, whose IT must approve calendar integrations

requests.text: A large deal that has not signed yet said "make scheduling frictionless or we're going elsewhere"
Requirements should call out that enterprise accounts need IT approval for calendar integrations

decisions.text: Scope this for the Q4 roadmap
Keep this in scope for scheduling, not calendar sync or other integrations
Prototype one flow next sprint to de-risk the API work

action_items.text: PM to add this to the strategy doc this week
PM to capture the enterprise IT approval point in the requirements

metrics_mentioned.text: 200 support tickets analysed from Q3; 45 of them (about 22%) were complaints about how long it takes to find a time
Customers say they spend 20+ minutes per meeting
3-4 back-and-forth messages per scheduled meeting, seen in the logs
Five customer interviews last month; all five said they waste time on calendar hunting
Three of the five interviewed customers said they are looking at competitors for this feature
Churn analysis: scheduling frustration is a leading indicator of churn in months 2-3 of onboarding
Engineer Lead estimate: 8 weeks, the absolute minimum for a good experience
